open-ax12 replaces the stock RadioMaster app. Only one app can talk to the radio at a time, so the stock app must be closed before this one starts.
If the status bar shows no link or the radio stays unavailable, force-stop the stock app in the Android settings and open open-ax12 again.
Everything that flies the model lives in the radio itself. The app edits that configuration and adds convenience on top: voice, vario tones, telemetry pages and logs.
Changes in Model setup are previewed live but are only kept after Save. Save writes them to the radio and stores the model in the library.
When you leave Model setup with unsaved changes the app asks whether to save, discard or stay.
System settings such as stick mode and alarm voltage are written at once. They are refused while the model has unsaved changes, so that a save never writes edits you did not mean to keep.
Flight modes, flaps and butterfly are compiled into ordinary mixes, curves and dual rates in the radio. They keep working if the app is closed.
Lines generated this way are marked as managed. Editing one by hand is allowed but the next compile will warn about it.
Voice announcements, the vario tone, logical switches and special functions run in the app. They cannot change channel outputs.
Text templates use names in braces, for example Battery {RxBt} volts. The speech engine and its language are set under System, Audio.
Telemetry comes from the receiver as CRSF frames. The Diagnostics screen shows which frame types arrive.
With the simulator backend the app runs without a radio. The simulator panel moves sticks, flips switches, sets telemetry and injects faults.
Diagnostics lists the open assumptions about the radio with the values needed to confirm them, and exports a report you can send along with a bug report.
Firmware updates are done in the stock RadioMaster app only. open-ax12 never updates the radio.
Always test control directions and failsafe with the motor disarmed after changing a model or restoring a backup.
